verdict_text:
NO

The artifact drops blocks `{2, 6, 10, 15}` instead of the specified `{2, 6, 10, 14}`, so it violates "Required result" clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14"). Consequently the kept set ends `..., 11, 12, 13, 14` and old block 14 is renumbered to 11, whereas clause 2 requires old 15 → 11; the final block's 15 tensors therefore carry the wrong weights, and grading against the hidden reference fails on bit-exact values. The required checks do not catch this: after renumbering all indices are 0..11, so "no tensor of blocks 12–15 remains" passes vacuously, and both the 12-block and 184-tensor counts hold for the wrong drop set as well. Everything else — pattern-based whole-block targeting, collision-free renumbering via a fresh output dict, preservation of the 4 non-block tensors, and the single output file at `out/T1/model.safetensors` — matches the specification.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
